brief: The FOMC unanimously hiked the fed funds rate 25bps to 3.75-4.00% on September 16, 2026, following a weak CPI print. The new Summary of Economic Projections implies a new reaction function: a materially higher policy rate path is now needed for the same 2027 inflation outcome as in June, underlined by an upward revision of the neutral rate to 3.2% from 3.1%. The Committee now expects two hikes in 2026 (versus one previously), a hold through 2027, and the first cut pushed to 2028, staying above neutral through 2029. Chair Warsh tied the shift to sticky inflation rather than unemployment (4.1%, called consistent with full employment), and said the hike cannot fix the underlying supply shock though it can prevent second-order effects. He gave no forward guidance. Rabobank still sees a "one and done" hike as more likely than a second one, contingent on Middle East developments and US economic resilience, and expects the Fed to cut sooner than its own projections show. Rabobank revises its house forecast to two cuts (Q4 2027, then 2028) and lifts its terminal rate call to 3.25-3.50% from 3.00-3.25%.
